articles.title: Luis Castro, Trish Reilly and Barry Wilkinson Named 2026 MacGuffin Award Honorees
articles.summary: The Property Masters Guild aims to highlight and elevate the craft of the Property Master by raising awareness, fostering collaboration among craft artisans, educating its members and inspiring future generations of Property Masters. The honorees, recognized for their craftsmanship,
body: Luis Castro, Trish Reilly and Barry Wilkinson will be honored at the third annual MacGuffin Awards.

Reilly is set to take home the Presidents Award for her career as a food stylist on titles like “Obi-Wan,” “Rebel Moon” and “The Orville,” as well as the culinary creations of “Grotesquerie” and drinkable blood for “American Horror Story.”

Wilkinson will be awarded the Lifetime Achievement Award after 40 years in the property department. He served as the property master of “Titanic,” “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom,” “Who Framed Roger Rabbit,” two James Bond films including “GoldenEye” and all eight of the original Harry Potter films.

“The MacGuffin Awards are about recognizing the people whose creativity, generosity and dedication help define our craft, both on set and beyond it,” said PMG President Jeffrey Johnson. “Luis, Trish and Barry each represent a different and invaluable part of what makes the property community so special. Their careers and contributions reflect the skill, ingenuity and spirit that we are proud to celebrate.”

articles.title: The Dog Stars review – Ridley Scott’s lethargic postapocalyptic drama is a misfire
articles.summary: An adaptation of Peter Heller’s 2012 novel never finds its footing with overly familiar survival beats and a glum lack of energy. Looking towards the end of an August movie dumping ground littered with more unwanted trash than usual, there seemed to be a faint glimmer of hope, a shiny treasure…
body: Hig’s belief that something more is out there causes him to leave for a nearby hub and, on the way, encounter a father-daughter pairing (Guy Pearce and Margaret Qualley) who end up joining him just as so-called “reapers” – essentially bloodthirsty goth invaders – come a’knocking.

It’s not that the action entering the fray so late into the movie is the problem here (I’m all for a more subdued character-based end-of-days drama a la Z for Zachariah ) or that the set pieces are all a little too cut-and-paste to truly excite (where the $110m budget went is a mystery). It’s that the plot and its characters are too maddeningly insubstantial to justify such human-over-spectacle storytelling.

articles.title: ‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Jacob Elordi’s Sensitive Survivalist Can’t Sustain a Dreary Dystopian Adventure
articles.summary: It’s the end of the world as we know it in “The Dog Stars,” and everyone feels — well, not fine exactly, but, you know, fine? Alive, hanging in there, taking it one day at a time. Things could be better, which goes without saying in the aftermath of a flu pandemic that has wiped
body: Four flu-pandemic survivors do the best they can in trying circumstances in Ridley Scott's low-energy latest, and the same goes for the charismatic quartet of actors muddling through it.

At its most interesting, “The Dog Stars” mimics the structure and stakes of a classic frontier Western, echoed quite literally in its two liveliest action setpieces: a briefly spectacular yet unperilous buffalo stampede, and a faceoff with a marauding tribe of feral, thickly made-up men on horseback, rather incuriously positioned by the film as an outright enemy force. The old-fashioned cowboys-and-Indians dynamic of this sequence is hard to ignore, as is the shared whiteness of the film’s leading characters: In this dog-eat-dog world, whose brutal survival strategies get to be heroic, and why?

articles.title: Lee Jung-eun, Kim Moo-yul Board Netflix’s Action-Noir Series ‘The Shooter’
articles.summary: Netflix has confirmed production on “The Shooter” (working title), an action-noir series that pairs Lee Jung-eun with Kim Moo-yul, marking Lee’s first outing in an action role. Lee’s turn comes on the heels of “My Daughter Is a Zombie,” one of South Korea’s top-grossing films of 2025.
body: “The Shooter” follows Jeong Suk-ja, a woman in her seventies whose quiet routine is shattered when her grandson is attacked, forcing her to pick up a firearm for the first time since she was young. Pursuing answers pulls her into the hidden workings of the powerful Chunghwa Group, and into a partnership she never expected, one that upends everything she believed to be true.
Kim plays Seo Yeon-woo, the strategist behind Jeong’s push for revenge, bringing a sharp eye for judgment and motives all his own.

Huh Joon-ho (“Notes from the Last Row,” “Mercy for None”) plays Jang Kwang-cheol, who once led the Heukseong Gang and has since risen to chair Chunghwa Group. Choi Sung-eun (“My Name Is Loh Kiwan,” “The Sound of Magic”) plays Shin Ji-hyun, who runs the company’s China office while overseeing Operations Unit 3. Bae Na-ra (“The WonderFools,” “Weak Hero Class 2”) plays Cheon Tae-seok, who assists the chairman while running Operations Unit 2. Seo Hyun-woo (“A Shop for Killers,” “Honour”) plays Yoo Il-koo, the Chunghwa Group outcast who oversees Operations Unit 4. Moon Jong-won rounds out the cast as Um Sang-pil, who runs a bed-and-breakfast and carries a past shrouded in mystery.

articles.title: Shin Mina, Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk, Lee Seyoung’s ‘The Remarried Empress’ Sets November Disney+ Bow
articles.summary: Disney+ has set a November premiere date for “The Remarried Empress,” a 10-part Korean drama adapted from the Naver Webtoon series of the same name, which has drawn nearly three billion views to date.
body: Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol adapted the series for the screen, with Cho Suwon (“Still 17,” “Pinocchio”) directing. The production was shot across multiple locations, including European palaces and other elaborate sets, according to Disney+.

The series will have its world premiere at the Busan International Film Festival in October, where it is set to screen three of its 10 episodes as part of the festival’s On Screen selection ahead of its full Disney+ rollout.
“The Remarried Empress” will roll out with a four-episode premiere on Nov. 4, then add two episodes each Wednesday until the series wraps with its finale on Nov. 25.

The series joins a slate of Korean Originals on Disney+ that includes “Made In Korea,” about a Korea CIA agent balancing underworld business dealings with a hunger for power; “Tempest,” centered on a global conspiracy threatening the Korean Peninsula; and “Moving,” which follows South Korean special agents protecting their super-powered children.

articles.title: John Irvin obituary
articles.summary: British film-maker and director of Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy who was described by Alec Guinness as having ‘balls behind the camera’ Bouncing from war zone reportage to cold war espionage, Hollywood horror to Sherwood Forest swashbuckler, Harold Pinter to Arnold Schwarzenegger, the director John…
body: “I’m a bit split,” he said. “I like playing with expensive toys, yet I also like the miniatures. I hate being pigeonholed, and I like to do the unexpected.”

He enjoyed his greatest success with the BBC mini-series Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (1979), adapted from John le Carré ’s novel about the intelligence officer George Smiley’s efforts to winkle out a Russian mole. Smiley was played with clenched elegance and economy by the formidable Alec Guinness, who took to striking out lines in the script whenever he felt he could convey the necessary information by expression alone.

“I was terrified, knowing I had to spend a year with him,” Irvin told Guinness’s biographer Piers Paul Read. On the first day of rehearsals, the director offered a suggestion that was rejected out of hand. After persuading Guinness to try the scene his way, Irvin was vindicated. “Very good, John,” the actor said. “Ten out of ten.”
points: “I like playing with expensive toys, yet I also like the miniatures.
I hate being pigeonholed, and I like to do the unexpected.”

articles.title: Ali G: Who Iz I? trailer reveals return of Sacha Baron Cohen’s prank-playing rudeboy
articles.summary: Comedian returns in new film, adding a retired US general to a list of pranked celebrities that include Buzz Aldrin and Donald Trump. The first full trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?
body: Sporting new dreadlocks but still wearing the clothing that was favoured by young white Britons copying US hip-hop and Black streetwear fashions in the 00s, Ali is back to contend with the issues of the day – as well as the pregnancy of his long-term girlfriend, Julie. In the 20 years since the character has been away, he says that “the world went to crap: there was Covid, wars and Ed Sheeran”.
The trailer gives glimpses of pranks played on retired US army general Stewart Rodeheaver, and someone who may be the Canadian DJ and producer Deadmau5 at a music festival.

Ali G first appeared on the UK comedy programme The 11 O’Clock Show in 1998, then in three series of Da Ali G Show in the early 00s, during which he interviewed unsuspecting politicians, academics, public figures and celebrities. He asked Buzz Aldrin if man will ever walk on the sun (perhaps during winter when it’s cold) and pitched a business idea for “ice-cream gloves” to Donald Trump. Da Ali G Show also featured the first appearances of Baron Cohen’s other best-known characters: the Kazakh TV reporter Borat Sagdiyev, and Brüno, an obtuse Austrian fashionista.
points: Comedian returns in new film, adding a retired US general to a list of pranked celebrities that include Buzz Aldrin and Donald Trump.

articles.title: Dolly Parton: A life in pictures
articles.summary: The singer rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world.
body: Over a career spanning more than 60 years, she sold more than 100 million records, wrote more than 3,000 songs and won 11 Grammy Awards, including a lifetime achievement honour.
Yet she has always described herself first and foremost as a songwriter. "It's my way of expressing myself. It's my therapy," she once said.
Dolly Parton grew up in poverty in a one-room cabin on the banks of the Little Pigeon River in Tennessee's Smoky Mountains, the fourth of 12 children.
She performed on local radio and television as a child and recorded her first single at 13.

articles.summary: Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, the singer's team announced on social media.
body: Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, her family announced on her social media.
"Sadness lies with us, not with Dolly," Parton's nephew Brian Seaver said in a video announcement.

articles.title: ‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Jacob Elordi and Margaret Qualley in Ridley Scott’s Subdued but Pleasingly Soulful Dystopian Western
articles.summary: Josh Brolin, Guy Pearce, Allison Janney and Benedict Wong also star in this adaptation of Peter Heller’s novel about survivors trying to stay alive in a post-apocalyptic future.
body: Elordi plays Hig, a widower inseparable from his loyal sidekick Jasper, a Belgian Malinois with him since the dog was a pup, and the most enduring link to happier times with Hig’s late wife, Melissa (Sai Bennett). Hig’s rapport is affectionate but spikier with tough military veteran Bangley ( Josh Brolin ), who despite his previous life in Army Aviation, never learned to fly. The two men share quarters in a converted hangar at an abandoned airstrip in Erie, Colorado, surrounded by a defensive perimeter.

Sharp-shooter Bangley takes care of weapons and fortifications, relying on Hig, a former mechanic and experienced pilot, to make reconnaissance flights in a battered Cessna to check for encroaching human threats and collect fuel and other supplies from what’s left of Denver. On one such mission, Hig learns of a new band of scavengers known as “Reapers,” reported to be more feral than any tribe before them, their sole purpose being to kill survivors and burn everything down.
points: Josh Brolin, Guy Pearce, Allison Janney and Benedict Wong also star in this adaptation of Peter Heller’s novel about survivors trying to stay alive in a post-apocalyptic future.

articles.title: Netflix Sets Lee Jung-eun, Kim Moo-yul for Korean Action-Noir Series ‘The Shooter’
articles.summary: From the director of ‘A Shop for Killers,’ the new series casts Lee Jung-eun, of 'Parasite' fame, as a woman in her 70s who is driven to pick up a gun after her grandson is attacked.
body: Netflix is adding to its already-packed Korean content slate with The Shooter, an action-noir series starring Lee Jung-eun and Kim Moo-yul. Revealing the project Wednesday, the streamer shared a photo of the cast from a recent table read in Seoul (above).

Directed by A Shop for Killers helmer Lee Kwon, The Shooter follows Jeong Suk-ja, a woman in her seventies living an ordinary life until an attack on her grandson sends her back to using a gun — something she hasn’t held since her youth. Hunting down the truth pulls her deeper into the secrets of the powerful Chunghwa Group — and into an unlikely partnership that complicates everything she thought she knew.

The ensemble also includes Huh Joon-ho as the former head of a criminal gang who has become chairman of Chunghwa Group, along with Choi Sung-eun, Bae Na-ra, Seo Hyun-woo and Moon Jong-won. Kim Hee-su wrote the series, which is produced by Studio Dragon.
